questions.stem: The principal function of the executive arm of government is to

options.text: make the laws of the state
implement and enforce the laws of the state
interpret the laws in cases of dispute
amend the constitution of the state

questions.explanation: A statute has no effect until an agency acts on it, and that execution is the whole purpose of the executive branch. Its other roles, such as policy initiation and appointment, exist to make that implementation possible.

distractorRationale.a: Law making belongs to the legislature, though the executive may initiate bills
distractorRationale.d: Constitutional amendment requires the legislature acting by a special majority

questions.stem: Which of the following belongs to the permanent executive?

options.text: A Permanent Secretary in a federal ministry

questions.explanation: A Permanent Secretary is a career civil servant who stays in office when governments change, providing continuity and technical advice. Ministers, commissioners and the Vice-President are political appointees who leave with the administration.

distractorRationale.a: A minister is a political appointee whose tenure ends with the government
distractorRationale.c: The Vice-President is elected on a political ticket and is part of the political executive
distractorRationale.d: A commissioner is the state-level equivalent of a minister and is equally political

questions.stem: An executive in which real power belongs to a Prime Minister while the Head of State performs only formal duties illustrates a

options.text: nominal executive alongside a real executive

questions.explanation: The ceremonial Head of State is the nominal executive and the Prime Minister is the real executive. Britain works this way, and so did Nigeria between 1963 and 1966 with President Azikiwe and Prime Minister Balewa.

distractorRationale.a: A plural executive vests authority in a council of equals, as in Switzerland
distractorRationale.c: A single executive combines both roles in one person, as Nigeria's President does today
distractorRationale.d: The permanent executive is the career civil service, not a division between head of state and head of government

questions.stem: The power of the President to pardon a convicted person or reduce a sentence is known as the
questions.explanation: The prerogative of mercy allows the executive to pardon, commute, remit or respite a punishment, and in Nigeria it is exercised after consultation with the Council of State. It is a check on the harshness of the criminal law rather than a review of the court's reasoning.

distractorRationale.b: Judicial review is a power of the courts over laws and official acts
distractorRationale.c: Delegated legislation is executive rule making under statutory authority
distractorRationale.d: Impeachment is the legislature's power to remove certain officeholders

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), section 175

questions.stem: Under the 1999 Constitution, the President is required to appoint at least one Minister from each state of the Federation. This requirement is an application of

options.text: the doctrine of separation of powers

questions.explanation: Federal character requires that the composition of government reflect the federal character of Nigeria, so that no state or section feels excluded from the centre. Guaranteeing every state a minister is the clearest statutory expression of the idea.

distractorRationale.b: The rule of law concerns government being bound by law, not the geographical spread of appointments
distractorRationale.c: Collective responsibility is a convention of the cabinet system
distractorRationale.d: Separation of powers concerns the relationship between the organs of government

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), sections 14 and 147

questions.stem: A plural executive is one in which executive authority is

options.text: vested in a single elected President
vested in a council or committee of equals
exercised entirely by career civil servants
shared between the central and state governments

questions.explanation: In a plural executive no single person is the chief executive; decisions are taken collectively by a council whose members are formally equal, as in Switzerland's Federal Council. The chairmanship may even rotate annually.

distractorRationale.a: That is a single executive, the Nigerian and American arrangement
distractorRationale.c: Civil servants form the permanent executive and act under political direction
distractorRationale.d: Sharing power between tiers describes federalism, not the form of the executive

questions.stem: The executive arm of government consists only of the President and the ministers.
questions.explanation: False. The executive also includes the permanent civil service, the police and armed forces, and the many parastatals, commissions and agencies that deliver public services. Those bodies carry out most of the actual implementation of policy.

distractorRationale.a: This confuses the political executive with the executive branch as a whole

questions.stem: When a minister issues regulations under powers granted to him by an Act of the National Assembly, he is exercising
questions.explanation: Parliament cannot foresee every technical detail, so it grants ministers and agencies power to fill in the detail by regulation. That rule making is delegated legislation, and it is one reason absolute separation of powers is impossible.

distractorRationale.b: Judicial review is the courts' power to test the validity of laws and official acts
distractorRationale.c: Oversight is the legislature scrutinising the executive, the reverse direction
distractorRationale.d: Appropriation is the legislature's authorisation of spending
